headline: Reverse a half, compare, then restore
statement: Determine whether a singly linked list reads identically forward and backward. Inputs use node-value arrays. The reference uses linear time and constant extra space. The reference restores its temporary link changes; input restoration is not an additional requirement for learner answers.
intuition: Compare the front half with the back half in reverse order. Find the middle, reverse the second half, and walk the two halves together. For an odd-length list, the middle value needs no comparison. Reverse the changed half again before returning to restore the input.
approach: Find the middle using slow and fast pointers.
Skip an odd center and reverse the second half.
Compare mirrored values, then reverse the suffix back before returning.
correctness: The reversed suffix visits the final nodes in exactly the order mirrored against the beginning. Every symmetric pair is compared; an odd center equals itself. Thus the comparisons are necessary and sufficient for a palindrome.
bruteForce: Copy values to an array and compare its forward and reverse orders, requiring O(n) extra space.

complexity.explanation: Finding the middle, reversing, comparing, and restoring each make linear scans using only pointers.

pitfalls: Save the next link before flipping it.
Restore the suffix before returning, including on mismatch.
